lean.fidelity_note: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer and $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. Assume $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$ for $j\ge1$. The formal statement proves $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for every $j\ge1$. The last formula is exactly (1.15), since $L_i=4\log\lambda_{i+1}$. The maximum is the greatest admissible integer. In the paper, $\mathcal B$ is also nondecreasing and dominates the fixed-order analytic constants, and $b$ is fixed by the later construction. The formal statement does not assume these two conditions; it proves the same three assertions from $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and the lower bound (1.13) alone. Frequencies are real, while derivative orders and the exponents $K(s)$ are nonnegative integers; the hypotheses force the relevant frequencies to be positive.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3
lean.plain: Divergence of the scheduled derivative orders
